text:
Clayton Kershaw debuts as lead analyst in Dodgers broadcast booth
LAX Leader
Los Angeles Dodgers legend Clayton Kershaw began a new chapter in his career on Aug. 26, serving as the lead analyst in the broadcast booth alongside play-by-play announcer Joe Davis. Kershaw, who retired from baseball only months ago, filled in for Orel Hershiser, Sportsnet LA’s main partner for Davis.
Kershaw had previously worked as a part-time sideline analyst for NBC’s “Sunday Night Baseball,” but this marked his first time taking on the primary analyst role during a live game broadcast. During the game, he provided insights into pitching strategies and shared stories from his playing days. His analysis extended beyond just Dodgers players; he also discussed Atlanta Braves pitcher Bryce Elder and their bullpen.
Kershaw offered commentary on pitchers’ approaches to challenging situations, stating that pitchers should not be afraid to use offspeed pitches even after throwing one in the dirt. He said it is important not to rely solely on fastballs during full counts because hitters expect them and are more likely to take a walk if challenged with predictable pitches.
He also commented on Tyler Glasnow’s return to starting after an extended absence, discussing what pitchers look for when coming back from injury or layoff. The article noted that while Hershiser brings old-school knowledge to broadcasts, Kershaw draws upon recent experience with current players and can speak about both modern analytics and traditional approaches.
Kershaw’s demeanor was described as enthusiastic and relaxed; he did not hesitate to laugh at himself or embrace unfamiliar aspects of broadcasting. The article suggested that if Hershiser needs time off in the future, Kershaw could reliably step into the role again. It concluded by noting that other networks may take interest in his potential as an analyst.
